purpose: A provenance-backed real ceramic motif reference and fired-photo cobalt mask for blue-and-white vessel synthesis.

source.title: Vase with dragon
source.medium: Porcelain painted in underglaze cobalt blue (Jingdezhen ware)

rights.basis: The Met object page labels the image Public Domain. The Met's Open Access API states that Open Access data and public-domain images are available for unrestricted commercial and noncommercial use without permission or fee.

downloaded_source_asset.source_status: Original Open Access image retained unchanged for computational motif reference and extraction; not a product-display asset.

semantic_motif_record.record_basis: The museum title identifies a dragon. Remaining visual observations below describe only what is visible in the selected O2 photograph and are not curatorial claims.
visible_body_parts_and_features: a prominent head facing toward the viewer's right
curved horn-like projections, an eye, a muzzle, whisker-like lines, and an open-looking jaw with tooth-like marks
a long sinuous body curling toward the viewer's left, with scale pattern visible on portions of the body
small projecting forms near the body that may be limbs or claws; their count and attachment are partly obscured by vessel curvature and the single camera view
motif_relations: the head and curling body read as one connected dragon motif across the broad shoulder/body in this view
dragon fragments at both image edges indicate continuation around the vessel circumference; the complete wrap is not recoverable from this single photograph

the whole-object view has a separate upper-neck register with blue scrolling forms and a geometric meander-like band; the Met record does not name these secondary forms, and they are outside the extracted crop
semantic_motif_record.layout_and_placement: The main dragon is painted as a broad horizontal, circumferential body decoration on the bulbous shoulder/body rather than as an isolated centered icon. The O2 photograph shows a front-facing projection with substantial curvature and side-wrap foreshortening.
semantic_motif_record.known_curatorial_meaning: The collection record names the motif as a dragon but gives no object-specific interpretation of its symbolic meaning.
unknown_or_not_asserted: symbolic or auspicious meaning of the dragon on this specific vase
whether the neck scrolls represent clouds or another named motif
the exact historical service, ritual, or display use of this vase
the unseen continuation and exact anatomy on the far side of the vessel

use_context.documented: The collection record titles and identifies the object as a vase and classifies it as ceramics.
use_context.specific_function: Not stated on the object record; no more specific use is inferred.

crop.description: Lossless crop centering the dragon on the vessel shoulder/body, with enough side area to show the motif wrapping around the curved form.

cobalt_mask.method: For each cropped RGB pixel, compute E = B - max(R,G), then output round(255 * clamp((E - 6)/(72 - 6), 0, 1)).
cobalt_mask.postprocessing: No blur, diffusion, inpainting, morphology, or semantic redraw is applied.

strong_cobalt_support_proxy.pixel_semantics: binary; 255 where B - max(R,G) >= 55 RGB units, else 0
strong_cobalt_support_proxy.intended_use: Optional sharper, hard-edged seed before applying a modeled diffusion step.
strong_cobalt_support_proxy.interpretation_limit: Thresholded high-chroma regions from the fired photograph, not a recovered pre-firing brush deposit.

derived_assets.interpretation_limit: The mask is a chroma-selected projection of the already-fired, photographed surface. It retains camera color, glaze response, illumination, photographic softness/compression, and curved-vessel projection. It is not recovered pre-firing brush placement or a measurement of physical pigment diffusion. Use it as a real motif/layout and visible-color seed for synthesis, not as a historical record of the initial deposit.
